key_insight: MANTRA reconstructs multiscale turbulent velocity fields from sparse, irregular measurements using a continuous representation constrained to a low-rank tensor manifold.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help recover detailed flow structures from limited experimental measurements without requiring gridded observations or governing equations.
method: Represent each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space.
Constrain coefficient tensors to low-rank Tucker manifolds and fit them with Riemannian optimization.
Adapt tensor rank and basis complexity to capture coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations.
evidence_signal: Tests on simulated isotropic turbulence and cylinder flow report reconstruction at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and robustness to Gaussian noise up to 20% of peak velocity; experimental jet data demonstrate recovery of time-evolving structures.
watch_item: Performance on other turbulent regimes and measurement patterns needs validation, particularly when low-rank structure is weak.
paper_title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data
